summary.text: Florence is the capital and most populous city of the Italian region of Tuscany.
Many academics consider it the birthplace of the Renaissance, when it became a major artistic, cultural, commercial, political, economic and financial center.
It was a centre of medieval European trade and finance, and its turbulent political history includes periods of rule by the powerful Medici family.

facts.label: Founded
facts.value: As a Roman garrison in 59 BC

facts.label: Money
facts.value: The gold florin financed industry all over Europe

facts.label: Language
facts.value: Its dialect forms the base of standard Italian

facts.label: National capital
facts.value: Capital of the Kingdom of Italy from 1865 to 1871

facts.label: Heritage
facts.value: UNESCO listed its Historic Centre in 1982

items.prompt: A student learning standard Italian today is learning something built on the speech of one Tuscan city. What made it the model?

options.label: The prestige of masterpieces by writers such as Dante, Petrarch and Boccaccio
A law that forced every region to adopt the city's dialect
The size of the city's population compared with all others
A treaty with the papacy that named it the official tongue

items.explain: The Florentine dialect became the language of culture throughout Italy because of the masterpieces by Dante, Petrarch, Boccaccio and others.

items.prompt: A king in 14th-century England needs money to fight a long war against France. Who might lend it?

options.label: The monks of Avignon, who held the largest treasury
Merchants of Turin, the capital at that time
Bankers from an Italian city whose gold coin financed Europe
Roman senators drawing on old imperial funds

items.explain: Florentine bankers financed the English kings during the Hundred Years' War, and Florentine money financed industry across Europe.

items.prompt: One Italian family produced two popes, a French regent and a French queen. What is the best description of that family?

options.label: A guild of Roman soldiers who settled the city
The Medici, one of European history's most important noble families
A line of Lombard rulers who conquered it under Charlemagne
A banking house that never held political office

items.explain: The Medici called Florence home; Leo X and Clement VII were popes, and Catherine and Marie de' Medici married French kings.

items.prompt: Italy's capital has not always been Rome. Which order of capitals fits the years after the kingdom was established in 1861?

options.label: Florence first, then Turin, then Rome
Rome first, then Florence, then Turin
Turin first, then Rome, then Florence
Turin first, then Florence, then Rome

items.explain: The Kingdom of Italy moved its capital from Turin to Florence in 1865, and the capital moved to Rome in 1871.

items.prompt: The Romans named their settlement Florentia, from a Latin verb meaning to blossom. What did the name mean?

options.label: The Army Camp
The Flourishing Town
The Town on the Arno
The Veterans' Fort

items.explain: Florentia meant "the Flourishing Town", from the Latin verb florere, to flourish or blossom.

items.prompt: What helped the early Roman settlement quickly become an important commercial centre?

options.label: It was the seat of the Medici bank from its earliest days
It was the only walled city between Turin and Rome
It sat on the main route between Rome and the north, in a fertile river valley
It sat beside the sea with the busiest port in Tuscany

items.explain: The settlement lay along the Via Cassia, the main route between Rome and the north, within the fertile valley of the Arno.
